# Fine-Tune Pipeline Design

**Date:** 2026-04-17
**Status:** Approved for planning
**Scope:** Build a reusable fine-tuning pipeline to LoRA-fine-tune four base VLMs (MedGemma 1.5 4B, Gemma 4 E4B, Qwen 3.5 4B, Qwen 3.5 9B) sequentially on the 28,486-entry structured-reasoning dataset generated by the Gemini 3.1 teacher pipeline.

---

## 1. Background and Motivation

### 1.1 Dissertation Context

The dissertation argues that Small Language Models (SLMs, 4–9 B parameters) can match or exceed general-purpose LLMs on specialised medical tasks when fine-tuned with structured reasoning distilled from a larger teacher model. Zero-shot baselines have been measured and published in `docs/src/implementation_log.md` Phase 7:

| Model | Params | Fitz17k Top-1 (LLM judge) | Gap to SkinFlow SOTA (29.19%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MedGemma 1.5 4B | 4 B | 22.22 % | 6.97 % |
| Qwen 3.5 9B | 9 B | 19.12 % | 10.07 % |
| Qwen 3.5 4B | 4 B | 14.61 % | 14.58 % |
| Gemma 4 E4B | 4.5 B eff. | 7.32 % | 21.87 % |

The fine-tuning work in this spec targets those gaps via a single supervised-fine-tuning (SFT) pass on structured reasoning, rather than SkinFlow's more expensive staged-RL approach.

### 1.2 Existing Upstream Artifacts

- `data/reasoning/reasoning.jsonl` — 28,486 entries produced by the Stage-1 observer (Gemini 3.0 Flash) and Stage-2 reasoner (Gemini 3.1 Pro) pipelines located in `src/train/observer/` and `src/train/reasoner/`.
- `data/reasoning/flagged.jsonl` — 139 entries where `label_match=false` was raised by the reasoner.
- `final/train/` (29,913 images, ~337 conditions) — lives on the user's local machine; **not currently on the RunPod network volume**, so a one-time sync is required.
- `src/train/reasoner/convert_to_training.py` — existing converter; will be superseded by `src/fine_tune/prepare_data.py` (see §3).
- `src/eval/` — working zero-shot evaluation pipeline on RunPod L40S with vLLM 0.19; the fine-tuned adapters will be re-run through this identical pipeline post-training.

### 1.3 Scope of this Spec

In scope:

- A reusable, config-driven fine-tuning package at `src/fine_tune/` that can train any of the four models via a YAML swap.
- Data preparation (stratified train/val split, unified output schema).
- RunPod operational scripts (sync, setup, run, resume).
- Artifact management (local checkpoints, HF Hub push of final adapters).

Out of scope (explicitly not this spec):

- Evaluation after training (re-uses existing `src/eval/` unchanged).
- Teacher-model re-generation or expansion of the 28 k training corpus.
- Mixing in external data sources (SkinCaRe, MM-Skin, Derm1M) — the user chose a single data source (Option A in Q3).
- Two-stage / staged-RL training — out of scope; single SFT pass only.
- Parallel multi-GPU training — one pod, one GPU per run, sequential.

## 2. High-Level Architecture

### 2.1 Package Layout (Repository)

```
src/fine_tune/
├── train.py                    # entrypoint: python -m fine_tune.train --config <path>
├── data.py                     # load train/val jsonl, image loader, collator
├── model_loader.py             # per-model HF load (model + processor + chat template)
├── callbacks.py                # HF Hub push callback, CSV logger
├── prepare_data.py             # reasoning.jsonl -> train.jsonl + val.jsonl (stratified 95/5)
├── configs/
│   ├── _template.yaml          # annotated reference (one-line comment per field)
│   ├── medgemma-1.5-4b.yaml
│   ├── gemma-4-e4b.yaml
│   ├── qwen3.5-4b.yaml
│   └── qwen3.5-9b.yaml
├── scripts/
│   ├── setup_pod.sh            # install CUDA deps, HF login, verify GPU
│   ├── sync_to_volume.sh       # rsync local data -> RunPod volume (one-time)
│   └── run.sh                  # wrapper: set env, call train.py with config
└── requirements-gpu.txt        # pins for transformers, peft, trl, accelerate, etc.
```

### 2.2 Runtime Layout (RunPod Network Volume)

```
/workspace/
├── dissertation/               # git clone of the repo
├── data/
│   ├── reasoning/
│   │   ├── reasoning.jsonl     # 28,486 entries from Gemini 3.1 (rsynced)
│   │   ├── train.jsonl         # ~27k stratified (output of prepare_data.py)
│   │   ├── val.jsonl           # ~1.4k stratified holdout
│   │   └── audit.jsonl         # 139 label_match=false entries (never trained on)
│   └── images/final/train/     # 29,913 images (rsynced once)
├── hf_cache/                   # HF model cache (HF_HOME); base weights persist across runs
└── runs/
    ├── manifest.csv            # one line per completed run (provenance ledger)
    └── <model-name>/
        ├── config.yaml         # exact config used for this run
        ├── checkpoint-epoch-N/ # LoRA adapter + optimizer state + RNG
        ├── final/              # best-by-eval-loss adapter (after load_best_model_at_end)
        ├── metrics.csv         # step-level train/eval loss log
        └── logs/               # TensorBoard event files
```

## 3. Data Preparation

### 3.1 `prepare_data.py` Responsibilities

Runs once (not per model), so all four models train on byte-identical data.

1. Read `data/reasoning/reasoning.jsonl`.
2. Filter: split out the 139 entries with `reasoning.label_match == false` into `audit.jsonl`. These stay out of training because the reasoner was forced to defend a label it suspected was wrong, so the reasoning signal is degraded.
3. Convert each remaining entry into chat format (see §3.3).
4. Stratified 95/5 split by `ground_truth`, `seed=42`, so every class (including rare ones like `seborrheic_dermatitis` and `lupus`) appears in both splits.
5. Write `train.jsonl` and `val.jsonl` to `/workspace/data/reasoning/`.
6. Print summary table: per-class counts in train/val, total examples, dropped-to-audit count.

### 3.2 Unified Assistant-Response Schema

Every assistant turn emits a single JSON object. This schema reconciles training with the existing evaluation pipeline.

```json
{
  "diagnosis": "basal cell carcinoma",
  "top_n": ["basal cell carcinoma", "squamous cell carcinoma",
            "seborrheic keratosis", "nevus"],
  "confidence": "high",
  "category": "malignant",
  "observation": {
    "morphology": "...",
    "color": "...",
    "texture": "...",
    "border": "...",
    "distribution": "..."
  },
  "reasoning": "Clinical reasoning paragraph tying features to diagnosis...",
  "differentials": [
    {"condition": "squamous cell carcinoma",
     "why_not": "SCC typically shows crust/ulceration rather than pearly..."}
  ]
}
```

Rationale for each field:

| Field | Consumer | Why present |
|---|---|---|
| `diagnosis` | Confusion Triads + Fitzpatrick17k scoring | Top-1 answer |
| `top_n` | Fitzpatrick17k Top-6 scoring | Differential list for containment matching |
| `confidence` | Reasoning-quality analysis | Calibration data |
| `category` | Multi-agent routing (future) | Inflammatory / malignant / benign / infectious |
| `observation` | Thesis narrative | Structured visual description as training signal |
| `reasoning` | MM-Skin VQA scoring (BERTScore) | Free-text diagnostic rationale |
| `differentials` | Safety analysis | Why-not explanations for the triad |

**`top_n` construction.** `top_n = [diagnosis] + [d.condition for d in differentials]`. The reasoner typically emits 3 differentials, so `top_n` is normally 4 entries. The eval scorer does containment matching and tolerates variable length; no padding is used. The key is renamed from `top_6` (eval's current field) to `top_n` to match the variable-length reality.

### 3.3 Chat Format

Each row in `train.jsonl` / `val.jsonl`:

```json
{"messages": [
  {"role": "user", "content": [
    {"type": "image", "image": "/workspace/data/images/final/train/lupus/lupus-chronic-cutaneous-13.jpg"},
    {"type": "text", "text": "Diagnose this skin condition with structured reasoning."}
  ]},
  {"role": "assistant", "content": "<unified JSON, serialized>"}
]}
```

Image paths are made absolute by `prepare_data.py` so the trainer never needs to know `image_root`; it only reads the paths as written.

### 3.4 Touch-Ups Outside the Fine-Tune Package

Two very small, backward-compatible edits to existing files:

1. `src/eval/score_results.py` — accept either `top_n` or `top_6` as the differentials key. ~5-line patch.
2. `src/train/reasoner/convert_to_training.py` — retained for git history; superseded in active use by `src/fine_tune/prepare_data.py`.

## 4. Per-Model YAML Config Schema

### 4.1 Annotated Reference (`configs/_template.yaml`)

```yaml
# ============================================================
# Fine-tune config template — copy & adjust per model.
# Field-by-field rationale inline.
# ============================================================

model:
  id: Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B                    # HuggingFace model ID of the base VLM to fine-tune
  trust_remote_code: true                # required for some VLM custom classes (Qwen VL, Gemma 3/4)
  torch_dtype: bfloat16                  # bf16 = half memory of fp32, no loss scaling needed (vs fp16)
  attn_implementation: flash_attention_2 # FA2 is 2-3x faster than sdpa on Ampere+; falls back if unavailable

lora:
  r: 64                                  # rank of LoRA decomposition; 64 is Skin-R1/DermoGPT standard
  alpha: 128                             # LoRA scaling factor; alpha=2*r is the PEFT rule of thumb
  dropout: 0.05                          # regularization on LoRA updates; 0.05 is standard for SFT
  bias: none                             # don't train bias terms; saves params with ~no accuracy cost
  target_modules:                        # which linear layers get LoRA adapters (names from named_modules)
    - q_proj                             # query projection in attention
    - k_proj                             # key projection in attention
    - v_proj                             # value projection in attention
    - o_proj                             # output projection after attention
    - gate_proj                          # gating projection in MLP (SwiGLU)
    - up_proj                            # up-projection in MLP (expansion)
    - down_proj                          # down-projection in MLP (contraction)
  modules_to_save: []                    # extra modules to train in full (e.g., "lm_head") — empty = LoRA-only
  freeze_vision_tower: true              # keep MedSigLIP / Qwen ViT frozen; train only language-side

training:
  output_dir: /workspace/runs/qwen3.5-9b # where checkpoints + logs land on the volume

  # --- Duration ---
  num_train_epochs: 5                    # 5 passes over 28k samples; cosine LR decays to ~0 by the end

  # --- Batch math ---
  per_device_train_batch_size: 1         # samples per GPU step (kept low for 9B + image tokens)
  gradient_accumulation_steps: 16        # steps before optimizer.step(); effective batch = 1 * 16 = 16

  # --- Optimizer ---
  learning_rate: 1.0e-4                  # peak LR; 1e-4 is standard PEFT/LoRA for VLMs
  warmup_ratio: 0.03                     # fraction of total steps for linear warmup (stabilizes early training)
  lr_scheduler_type: cosine              # cosine decay from peak to ~0; smooth landing, no rude drop
  optim: paged_adamw_8bit                # 8-bit AdamW with pageable states; saves ~30% memory (9B only)
  weight_decay: 0.01                     # mild L2 regularization on non-LoRA weights (mostly no-op here)

  # --- Precision + memory ---
  bf16: true                             # compute in bfloat16; must match torch_dtype
  gradient_checkpointing: true           # trades recompute for memory; ~30% slower, ~40% less VRAM

  # --- Logging / eval / save ---
  logging_steps: 10                      # log loss every N steps; shows training curve live
  eval_strategy: steps                   # run val loop at step intervals (not per-epoch)
  eval_steps: 200                        # every 200 steps (~once per 10-15 min on 9B)
  save_strategy: epoch                   # checkpoint at end of each epoch
  save_total_limit: 3                    # keep only the 3 most recent epoch checkpoints to save disk
  load_best_model_at_end: true           # after training, reload the epoch with lowest val loss
  metric_for_best_model: eval_loss       # criterion for "best checkpoint"
  greater_is_better: false               # lower eval_loss is better

  # --- Reproducibility ---
  seed: 42                               # same seed across models = identical data shuffle

  # --- Monitoring ---
  report_to: [tensorboard]               # TB event files in output_dir/runs; csv log also on volume

data:
  train_file: /workspace/data/reasoning/train.jsonl  # prepared jsonl with absolute image paths
  val_file:   /workspace/data/reasoning/val.jsonl    # 5% stratified holdout
  max_seq_length: 4096                   # hard cap on tokenized sample length; truncates if over
  image_max_pixels: 1048576              # resize guard (≈1024x1024) so image tokens don't explode

hub:
  repo_id: danielfdias98/qwen3.5-9b-derm-reasoning  # HF Hub repo to push final adapter to
  push_strategy: end                     # push only the best checkpoint at run end (not per-epoch)
  private: true                          # keep unpublished until dissertation-ready
```

### 4.2 Per-Model Deltas

The four config files vary only in the fields below; everything else is held constant to keep cross-model comparisons fair.

| Field | MedGemma 1.5 4B | Gemma 4 E4B | Qwen 3.5 4B | Qwen 3.5 9B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `model.id` | `google/medgemma-1.5-4b-it` | `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` |
| `per_device_train_batch_size` | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| `gradient_accumulation_steps` | 8 | 8 | 8 | 16 |
| `optim` | `adamw_torch` | `adamw_torch` | `adamw_torch` | `paged_adamw_8bit` |
| `output_dir` | `/workspace/runs/medgemma-1.5-4b` | `/workspace/runs/gemma-4-e4b` | `/workspace/runs/qwen3.5-4b` | `/workspace/runs/qwen3.5-9b` |
| `hub.repo_id` | `danielfdias98/medgemma-1.5-4b-derm-reasoning` | `danielfdias98/gemma-4-e4b-derm-reasoning` | `danielfdias98/qwen3.5-4b-derm-reasoning` | `danielfdias98/qwen3.5-9b-derm-reasoning` |

Effective batch size = 16 across all four configs (bs × grad_accum). LoRA rank, LR, epoch count, warmup, scheduler, seed, and val split are identical everywhere.

### 4.3 Open Items Resolved at Implementation Time

- **Exact `target_modules`** — verified per model by dumping `model.named_modules()` before committing each YAML. Qwen and Gemma families share the same 7-name convention; MedGemma 1.5 is Gemma-3-based and expected to match.
- **`attn_implementation`** — tested on the first model trained. If the FA2 wheel doesn't match the pod's CUDA, fall back to `sdpa` (same correctness, slightly slower).

## 5. Training Loop

### 5.1 `model_loader.py`

Three responsibilities:

1. **Load the right class** via `transformers.AutoConfig` dispatch:
   - Qwen 3.5 VL → `AutoModelForVision2Seq`
   - MedGemma 1.5 / Gemma 4 → `AutoModelForImageTextToText`
   - Fallback → `AutoModelForCausalLM` (not expected for any of the 4 configured models)
2. **Load processor + chat template** — `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model.id)` returns the family-specific processor with its chat template already wired. No manual templating code.
3. **Apply LoRA** — wrap with `peft.get_peft_model(base, LoraConfig(...))`. When `freeze_vision_tower: true`, iterate `named_parameters()` and set `requires_grad=False` on any parameter whose name contains `vision_tower`, `vision_model`, or `visual` (matches Qwen, MedGemma, and Gemma naming).

Returns `(model, processor)`.

### 5.2 `data.py`

- **Dataset**: `datasets.load_dataset("json", data_files=...)`. Each row is chat-format from `prepare_data.py`. Lazy loaded — 28 k image paths fit RAM easily; images themselves are loaded per batch inside the collator.
- **Collator**: loads PIL images from paths in the user turn, applies `processor.apply_chat_template(..., tokenize=True, return_dict=True)`, returns `input_ids`, `attention_mask`, `labels`, `pixel_values`. Masks user-turn tokens to `-100` in `labels` so the loss is computed only over the assistant response. This is critical: without masking, the model learns to predict the prompt, which wrecks gradient signal.

Pattern works across all 4 models because the processor abstracts format differences.

### 5.3 `train.py`

~120 lines, linear flow:

```
1. Parse --config path, load YAML into a dataclass
2. Seed everything (torch, numpy, random, transformers.set_seed)
3. HF login from env var HF_TOKEN
4. Load model + processor via model_loader
5. Apply LoRA via peft.get_peft_model
6. Load train + val datasets via data.py
7. Build collator bound to the processor
8. Construct TrainingArguments from config.training
9. Instantiate trl.SFTTrainer (fallback: transformers.Trainer if TRL multimodal SFT is unstable in our TRL version)
10. Attach callbacks: HFHubPushCallback, CSVLoggerCallback
11. trainer.train(resume_from_checkpoint=args.resume)
12. trainer.save_model(output_dir/"final")          # best-adapter (load_best_model_at_end already reloaded it)
13. Push to Hub (callback handles this at on_train_end)
14. Append provenance row to /workspace/runs/manifest.csv
15. Print final metrics + adapter path + HF repo URL
```

### 5.4 Callbacks

- **`HFHubPushCallback`** — on `on_train_end`, calls `trainer.model.push_to_hub(repo_id, private=True, commit_message=f"epoch {best_epoch}, eval_loss {loss:.4f}")`. PEFT's `push_to_hub` uploads only the adapter (~100-400 MB), never base weights. Also uploads an auto-generated `README.md` (model card) and the `config.yaml` used for the run.
- **`CSVLoggerCallback`** — writes one row per log step to `output_dir/metrics.csv` with `step, train_loss, eval_loss (if present), lr`. Redundant with TensorBoard, but trivially parseable for dissertation results tables.

### 5.5 Edge-Case Handling

1. **OOM on Qwen 3.5 9B.** If bf16 + FA2 + gradient-checkpointing still OOMs at bs=1: (a) drop `max_seq_length` to 3072, (b) bump `optim` to `paged_adamw_8bit` (already the default for 9B), (c) QLoRA (4-bit base) as last resort. A `--dry-run` mode in `train.py` runs one forward/backward before the full run to detect OOM early.
2. **Image path not found.** Collator raises `FileNotFoundError` with the offending path — easier to debug than silent skip.
3. **Pod restart mid-run.** `trainer.train(resume_from_checkpoint=True)` auto-detects the latest `checkpoint-*` in `output_dir`. Optimizer state, scheduler, LoRA weights, and RNG all restored. Exposed via `--resume` on `train.py`.

---

## 6. Checkpointing and Artifact Flow

### 6.1 During Training

Every epoch the Trainer writes to `/workspace/runs/<model-name>/checkpoint-<step>/`:

```
checkpoint-1773/
├── adapter_config.json        # PEFT metadata
├── adapter_model.safetensors  # LoRA weights only (~100-400 MB, not the base)
├── optimizer.pt               # AdamW state — needed for resume
├── scheduler.pt               # LR schedule state
├── trainer_state.json         # step count, log history, best metric
├── training_args.bin          # TrainingArguments snapshot
└── rng_state.pth              # numpy/torch/cuda RNGs for deterministic resume
```

`save_total_limit: 3` keeps only the 3 most recent; older ones auto-deleted.

### 6.2 Disk Budget

Base weights stay in `/workspace/hf_cache/` (one-time download per model, reused across runs).

| Artifact | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen 3.5 9B base weights | ~18 GB | bf16 |
| Qwen 3.5 4B base weights | ~8 GB | bf16 |
| MedGemma 1.5 4B base weights | ~8 GB | bf16 |
| Gemma 4 E4B base weights | ~9 GB | bf16 |
| One epoch checkpoint | ~300 MB adapter + ~1 GB optimizer | × 3 rolling = ~4 GB/run |
| Final adapter (post-load-best) | ~300 MB | One per model |
| **All 4 models cached + in-flight** | **~60 GB** | Fits a standard 100–200 GB RunPod volume |

### 6.3 Best-Checkpoint Selection

`load_best_model_at_end: true` + `metric_for_best_model: eval_loss` + `greater_is_better: false` means the Trainer reloads whichever epoch had the lowest validation loss, then `trainer.save_model(output_dir/"final")` serialises that as the canonical adapter for the run.

### 6.4 HF Hub Push (End-of-Run Only)

The `HFHubPushCallback.on_train_end` uploads to `danielfdias98/<model-name>-derm-reasoning` (private):

```
danielfdias98/qwen3.5-9b-derm-reasoning/
├── adapter_config.json
├── adapter_model.safetensors
├── README.md                  # auto-generated: model ID, hyperparams, split sizes, best eval_loss, wall-clock, commit SHA
└── config.yaml                # the exact training recipe
```

Re-running evaluation later becomes three lines:

```python
from peft import PeftModel
base = load_base(config.model.id)
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base, "danielfdias98/qwen3.5-9b-derm-reasoning")
```

### 6.5 Provenance Ledger

Every completed run appends one row to `/workspace/runs/manifest.csv`:

| timestamp | model | config_sha | best_epoch | eval_loss | wall_clock_hours | hub_repo |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-04-18T14:22 | qwen3.5-9b | a3f2c1 | 4 | 0.832 | 9.4 | danielfdias98/qwen3.5-9b-derm-reasoning |

This becomes a table in the dissertation's fine-tuning chapter — each run captured as a single reproducible record.

---

## 7. RunPod Operations

### 7.1 Pod Specification

| Resource | Spec | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| GPU | L40S (48 GB) | Same class as eval pod; Qwen 9B + LoRA + FA2 fits at bs=1 / GA=16 |
| Image | `runpod/pytorch:2.4.0-py3.11-cuda12.4-devel-ubuntu22.04` (or newer) | Matches wheels for FA2, bitsandbytes, recent transformers |
| Volume | Existing network volume (100+ GB), mounted at `/workspace` | Holds data, checkpoints, HF cache across pod restarts |
| Env vars | `HF_TOKEN` (write-scoped), `HF_HOME=/workspace/hf_cache` | Hub auth + persistent cache |

### 7.2 `scripts/sync_to_volume.sh` — One-Time Upload

Runs from the user's laptop (training images and `reasoning.jsonl` are not yet on the volume).

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Uploads final/train/ (29,913 images) + data/reasoning/reasoning.jsonl to the RunPod volume.
# Assumes RunPod SSH config is set up (re-uses the setup from the eval phase).
set -euo pipefail

POD_ALIAS="${POD_ALIAS:-runpod-train}"
REMOTE_ROOT="/workspace/data"

rsync -avz --progress --partial \
  final/train/ \
  "${POD_ALIAS}:${REMOTE_ROOT}/images/final/train/"

rsync -avz --progress \
  data/reasoning/reasoning.jsonl \
  "${POD_ALIAS}:${REMOTE_ROOT}/reasoning/reasoning.jsonl"

echo "Sync complete. Log in and run: python -m fine_tune.prepare_data"
```

Idempotent (rsync skips unchanged).

### 7.3 `scripts/setup_pod.sh` — Once Per Fresh Pod

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

export HF_HOME=/workspace/hf_cache
mkdir -p /workspace/hf_cache /workspace/runs

pip install --upgrade \
  'transformers>=4.48' \
  'peft>=0.13' \
  'trl>=0.13' \
  'accelerate>=1.2' \
  'bitsandbytes>=0.44' \
  'datasets>=3.0' \
  'flash-attn>=2.6' --no-build-isolation \
  'pillow' 'pyyaml' 'tensorboard'

if [ -z "${HF_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: HF_TOKEN env var not set"; exit 1
fi
huggingface-cli login --token "${HF_TOKEN}" --add-to-git-credential

python -c "import torch; print(f'CUDA: {torch.cuda.is_available()}, GPUs: {torch.cuda.device_count()}')"
ls /workspace/data/reasoning/reasoning.jsonl >/dev/null && echo "Data OK"
```

### 7.4 `scripts/run.sh` — Per-Model Run

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: ./scripts/run.sh configs/qwen3.5-9b.yaml [--resume]
set -euo pipefail
CONFIG="${1:?usage: run.sh <config> [--resume]}"
shift || true
export HF_HOME=/workspace/hf_cache
cd /workspace/dissertation
python -m fine_tune.train --config "${CONFIG}" "$@"
```

### 7.5 End-to-End Procedure

**One-time setup:**

1. Provision L40S pod with the existing network volume mounted.
2. On laptop: `./scripts/sync_to_volume.sh` — ~30 minutes for 29 k images.
3. SSH into pod, `git clone` the repo to `/workspace/dissertation`.
4. `HF_TOKEN=<token> bash scripts/setup_pod.sh` — ~10 minutes.
5. `python -m fine_tune.prepare_data` — produces `train.jsonl` + `val.jsonl`, ~1 minute.

**Per-model run (repeat 4×):**

```bash
bash scripts/run.sh configs/medgemma-1.5-4b.yaml   # ~6–8 h estimate
bash scripts/run.sh configs/qwen3.5-9b.yaml        # ~10–14 h estimate
bash scripts/run.sh configs/qwen3.5-4b.yaml        # ~5–7 h estimate
bash scripts/run.sh configs/gemma-4-e4b.yaml       # ~6–8 h estimate
```

Exact times confirmed after the first run; used to budget the remaining three.

**Pod restart / migration mid-run:**

1. Restart pod with the same volume.
2. If deps evaporated: `HF_TOKEN=<token> bash scripts/setup_pod.sh`.
3. `bash scripts/run.sh configs/<current>.yaml --resume` — picks up from latest checkpoint, zero data loss.

**After a run finishes:**

Adapter is on HF Hub + the volume. Stop the pod immediately to halt billing. Data and HF cache persist for the next run.

### 7.6 Budget

- L40S on-demand ≈ US$0.70–1.00 / hour (reference price; verify in dashboard at run time).
- ~35 training hours (all 4 models) + ~10 post-training eval hours + slack = **US$50–100** of GPU budget for the full sweep.
- Stop pod between runs to avoid idle charges. `runpodctl` can automate start/stop if desired (not required for the first run).

---

## 8. Hyperparameter Rationale Summary

| Choice | Value | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| LoRA rank `r` | 64 | Skin-R1 (arXiv:2511.14900) and DermoGPT (arXiv:2601.01868) both use r=64 and report strong dermatology results |
| LoRA `alpha` | 128 | PEFT convention `alpha = 2r`; scales LoRA contribution appropriately |
| Epochs | 5 | 28 k samples × 5 ≈ 140 k example-passes; cosine decays cleanly by end |
| Peak LR | 1e-4 | Standard VLM PEFT/LoRA rate; low enough for stable adaptation, high enough to move in 5 epochs |
| Warmup | 3 % of steps | Small linear warmup prevents early instability |
| Scheduler | Cosine | Smooth decay to near-zero by end-of-training; well-behaved |
| Effective batch | 16 | Balance of throughput vs stability on a single 48 GB GPU with image tokens |
| Seed | 42 | Identical data shuffle across all 4 models → fair comparison |
| Vision tower | Frozen | 28 k is too small to retrain; preserves MedSigLIP's medical advantage on MedGemma; avoids degradation of Qwen VL's early-fusion features |

---

## 9. Success Criteria

The pipeline is successful when:

1. A fresh L40S pod, following §7.5 verbatim, completes at least one full fine-tuning run without manual intervention beyond supplying `HF_TOKEN`.
2. The resulting LoRA adapter loads cleanly via `PeftModel.from_pretrained(base, hub_repo)` and produces valid JSON (per the schema in §3.2) on `src/eval/` benchmarks.
3. Fine-tuned `eval_loss` at the best epoch is lower than at step 0 (trivial sanity check the model is learning).
4. The four YAML configs are swap-and-run — changing `--config` is the only action required to train a different model.
5. `manifest.csv` captures one row per completed run with all fields populated.
6. Re-running the same config produces identical `train.jsonl` / `val.jsonl` (determinism) and identical training curves ±noise (reproducibility).

These criteria are verifiable without interpreting benchmark accuracy. Accuracy improvement vs. zero-shot baselines (the actual thesis contribution) is measured afterwards by re-running `src/eval/` and is out of scope for this spec.

---

## 10. Non-Goals

For clarity, these are explicitly **not** part of this spec:

- Multi-GPU / distributed training (DeepSpeed, FSDP, ZeRO).
- QLoRA 4-bit by default (only an OOM fallback for 9B if needed).
- Wiring any external data (SkinCaRe, MM-Skin, Derm1M).
- Two-stage training or reinforcement learning (SkinFlow-style).
- UI / dashboard / live monitoring beyond TensorBoard + CSV.
- Post-training model merging or adapter stacking.
- Fine-tuning the vision tower.
